observations: fabro-56f4 basis verified fresh against the current tree: `tester -> implementer [label="Gate red"]` exists at `.fabro/workflows/develop/workflow.fabro:263`, referenced known-bug seed fabro-febd is still open, and no seed-matching mechanism exists anywhere in the develop workflow.

Engine primitives for this seed already exist and need no engine changes: command nodes store stdout in context (default `command.output`, custom `output.*` keys via structured output, see `lib/components/fabro-workflow/src/handler/command.rs`), and a later script node can read a prior node's output via `stdin_source` + ref resolution (closeout pattern).

There is no cheap host-side way to validate an edited `.fabro` graph: no `fabro` binary on PATH and no test that parses the repo's own workflows, so verifying `workflow.fabro` after an edit required writing a temporary integration test in `lib/components/fabro-validate` (cold build ~7 min) and deleting it after. A `just validate-workflows` recipe (parse + built_in_rules over `.fabro/workflows/**/*.fabro`) would make every platform seed's graph edits cheaply checkable and would have caught nothing-but-syntax drift here in seconds.

Matching-generics pitfall measured while tuning gate-bounce.nu: counting bare alphabetic tokens ≥6 chars (`server`, `target`, `render`, `returns`) from seed prose produced 2 false-positive seed matches against an unrelated fabro-febd tail (fabro-5453, fabro-0195); restricting to separator/digit-bearing compounds (or words ≥12 chars) eliminated all false positives while keeping fabro-febd's signature match — relevant for any future deterministic-log-matching heuristic.
